en.title: Maximum Smooth Substring Score After Changing One Letter
en.description:
A non-empty contiguous substring contributes 1 point if every pair of adjacent characters differs by at most 1 in alphabet position; a single character contributes 1 point in total. You may change at most one character of the original string to any lowercase letter; find the highest total score. The condition only constrains adjacent characters; it does not require the difference between the largest and smallest letters of the whole segment to be ≤1.

The standard I/O, examples and solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: One line with a lowercase string. The original snapshot gives no length bound; this site sets 1≤length≤100000.
en.explanation: Example 1: changing c to b gives aababfgh; the first segment of length 5 contributes 15 and the last segment of length 3 contributes 6, for a total of 21. Example 2: the whole string is already smooth, so all 10 substrings score. Example 3: changing e to a gives abaz; the first three characters contribute 6 and z contributes 1, for a total of 7.
hints: Precompute, for each position, the maximum smooth contiguous length extending left and right. A change only affects the substrings containing that position; enumerate the 26 replacements and compute the new (left extension+1)(right extension+1) minus the old contribution.
